candidates.lead: The funeral of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston will take place in Wigan later
candidates.evidence_text: Billy Boston funeral to take place - BBC News Image source, PA Image caption, Sir Billy Boston died in August aged 92. By Jenny Coleman North West Published 1 hour ago The funeral of rugby league legend Sir Billy Boston will take place later. Boston, who was the first player in rugby league's 130-year history to receive a knighthood, died last month aged 92. His funeral will take place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium at 12:30 BST, with a limited number of supporters able to attend. Before the service, a cortege will travel through Wigan , external and arrive at the stadium. The West Stand will be open as Sir Billy makes his final journey through the Stadium Tunnel. A private burial will follow. To play this video you need to enable JavaScript in your browser. This video can not be played Figure caption, Boston is regarded as one of Britain's truly great rugby league players At the request of the Boston family, people attending are being encouraged to wear traditional funeral attire, but items of Wigan Warriors' cherry red can be worn such as scarves, ties and headwear. People are welcome to pay their respects to the funeral cortege, which will follow a route through Wigan. Born in Cardiff in 1934, Boston grew up playing union but was overlooked by his home club. He came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old. He was picked for the 1954 Great Britain side and was the first black British player to tour Australia and New Zealand. He reached the 100-try milestone in just 68 matches and claimed 478 tries in 488 games for Wigan, helping them win three Challenge Cups and the Championship. In all, Boston scored 571 tries in his career - a total surpassed only by Australian legend Brian Bevan in top-class rugby league - and is one of the truly great British rugby league players. candidates.lead: The walkways will connect parts of Manchester city centre to other places, including the Etihad campus
candidates.evidence_text: Etihad plan part of £100m 'floating walkways' scheme - BBC News Image caption, The CyanLines project will see a number of "floating walkways" connecting different parts of Manchester By Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 1 hour ago Plans for a "floating walkway" linking Manchester city centre to the Etihad campus have been revealed. It will be part of the £100m CyanLines plan to create a 100-mile (161km) network of walkways around the Greater Manchester region over the next decade. The recently announced route will see the Etihad campus - home to Manchester City FC - connected to Piccadilly station, taking in Ashton Canal, New Islington and Holt Town. Greater Manchester mayor Bev Craig said: "It's not just about travel, the whole point of CyanLines is 100 miles of nature connected together, and yes it's about how you move, cycle and walk, but it's something more fundamental." There are two further CyanLines routes in development in Newton Heath and Rusholme. Backing for the plans comes from the Manchester and Trafford councils, the Greater Manchester Combined Authority, Manchester City FC, the Canal and River Trust, property developers Renaker and Urban Splash, and the National Trust, among others. Pete Bradshaw, director of sustainability at Manchester City, said: "The plans for the CyanLines route add a new layer of nature-rich, innovative and imaginative active travel and community experiences for fans, visitors and those living and working in the neighbourhood." Image caption, The next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct park project has also been announced Funding for the next phase of the Castlefield Viaduct "garden in the sky" was also announced. Part of the old railway line has been transformed into a public park, which opened in 2022. The second phase will expand it to the full 330-metre length of the Victorian-era structure. It is being supported by the Bupa Foundation's Healthy Cities programme. Hilary McGrady, director-general at the National Trust, said: "Bupa's funding will help the Trust extend the sky park project in Manchester, meaning more people will experience and benefit from this green space that sits in the heart of the city." candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Council condemns attacks on bin crews and traffic wardens - BBC News Image source, LDRS Image caption, A bin wagon had a brick thrown through a side window while out on its rounds in Oldham By Ed Barnes Local Democracy Reporting Service Published 9 September 2026 Targeting bin crews and traffic wardens out doing their jobs is "unacceptable", a council has said, after a wagon had a brick thrown through its window while out on its rounds. At least one traffic warden was also said to have been targeted in the Goldwick area, Oldham Council said. Speaking after the bin wagon incident last month, a spokesperson said the wagon had its driver-side window smashed "by a resident" and a parking enforcement officer was subjected to abuse. "Our staff are working hard every day to deliver essential services for communities across the borough. These unacceptable actions not only put people at risk but also delay services for other residents," they added. The council has recently laid fresh double yellow lines and given out 273 parking fines so far this year in parts of the Waterloo Street area. "Enforcement officers are carrying out their duties to help keep our highways safe and accessible," the council continued. "Any form of verbal or physical abuse towards our staff is completely unacceptable and will not be tolerated." candidates.evidence_text: Manchester house explosion leaves man critically injured - BBC News Image source, Victor Olowoyo Image caption, A man is in a critical condition after an explosion at a house in Harpurhey By Lauren Hirst and Haider Saleem , North West Published 8 September 2026 A man is fighting for his life in hospital following a house explosion in Manchester. Fire crews and police were called to Ash Street in the Harpurhey area following the blast at about 10:20 BST. Greater Manchester Police said the man was critically injured and taken to hospital. Neighbouring properties were evacuated and a woman was also treated for what police said were thought to be minor injuries. Ash Street and Rochdale Road were closed and people have been urged to avoid the area. Image caption, Roads around the area had been cordoned off Neighbour Linda Kay, who has lived in the area for 28 years, said she thought a "bomb had gone off". "I was upstairs. I was supposed to be going on holiday this afternoon so my head was elsewhere," said the 68-year-old. "I've come down. I've just seen everything here and I thought 'my god what's happening'. "The ambulance driver came over and said there's been a really, really bad explosion. "I thought a bomb had gone off. "I did think it was bomb situation with all the response. It was quite scary." Image caption, A woman was also injured in the explosion Georgia, 16, said the explosion "shook the whole house and [there was] a massive bang". "It sounded like a car went straight through the front window," she said. "The police told me to exit my house as they didn't know whether it was safe or not." Phil Hendrick, head of North West operational delivery at gas infrastructure firm Cadent, said it was "too early to confirm a cause". "We are on site in Ash Street assisting fire and other emergency services, which is routine for an incident of this nature," he said. "Our job in an incident like this is to ensure everything associated with gas is safe. "Although it is too early to confirm a cause, there is nothing at this stage to suggest any issues with the local gas network." candidates.lead: A replacement queen is being introduced after vandals overturned a community beehive
candidates.evidence_text: Ashton-under-Lyne queen bee killed in hive vandalism - BBC News Image source, Chris Place Image caption, Chris said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever the hive over By Haider Saleem Reporting from North West Published 9 September 2026 A queen bee was killed when vandals damaged a community hive that had been set up on a playing field. Chris Place, 74, said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever over the hive at King George V Playing Fields in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester. He said volunteers had spent the past year growing the thriving colony, but were now having to try to introduce a replacement queen. Volunteers said the damage happened between 17:30 BST on 5 September and 08:30 the following morning. Place, a volunteer beekeeper, said the hive's metal stand was buried about 18in (46cm) into the ground but appeared to have been levered upwards using bricks and wooden poles. Branches had also been taken from a nearby dead hedge and used to strike the hives, he said. Image caption, About seven regular volunteers help care for the bees at the community apiary Place added: "People might think it's just a wooden box that's been knocked over. It isn't. It's a living colony containing thousands of bees." He said an inspection afterwards found the queen was missing and the bees had begun producing queen cells, which indicated the colony had become queenless. Image source, Chris Place Image caption, The damaged hive contained a colony of thousands of bees Place said he had found a replacement queen costing about £50, which volunteers would carefully introduce to the colony. "If they accept her, we've got a fighting chance," he said, adding that the colony could otherwise be lost. "All the volunteers were very proud of what we've achieved there and now it's just been destroyed," Place said. Image source, Chris Place Image caption, The apiary, bottom left, is based within King George V Playing Fields in Ashton-under-Lyne and is surrounded by a 7 foot high fence with like spikes He said six or seven regular volunteers helped care for the apiary, which is a community rather than commercial project. Honey produced by the bees is sold through the site's Georgie Porgies café to help raise funds. Place said a hive was also vandalised at the site last year, although volunteers were able to put it back together. He said bees already faced threats from parasites, disease, wasps and Asian hornets. "They've got enough challenges without humans deliberately creating another one," he said. Image source, Chris Place Image caption, Several colonies are kept at the community apiary at King In a letter seen by the BBC, local MP Angela Rayner said she was "horrified" by the vandalism and described it as "something so mindless". She offered her support to the volunteers and said she would like to visit the project. The Friends group has appealed for anyone who may have witnessed suspicious activity around the hives to come forward. candidates.evidence_text: A queen bee was killed when vandals damaged a community hive that had been set up on a playing field Chris Place, 74, said bricks and wooden poles appeared to have been used to lever over the hive at King George V Playing Fields in Ashton-under-Lyne, Greater Manchester He said volunteers had spent the past year growing the thriving colony, but were now having to try to introduce a replacement queen Volunteers said the damage happened between 17:30 BST on 5 September and 08:30 the following morning Place, a volunteer beekeeper, said the hive's metal stand was buried about 18in (46cm) into the ground but appeared to have been levered upwards using bricks and wooden poles Branches had also been taken from a nearby dead hedge and used to strike the hives, he said

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform boss says he's still in charge despite claims he is being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader and other party leaders were rep Oldham Reform’s boss says claims he is no longer in the post are ‘just gossip and hearsay’. This comes two days after other party leaders were reportedly told Councillor Lewis Quigg was being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader in the borough. However, Coun Quigg has denied the claims, initially telling the Manchester Evening News he would not ‘confirm nor deny silly allegat He later said the claims are ‘just nonsense really’ and ‘just gossip and hearsay’. When asked to confirm whether he was still leader on September 9, Coun Quigg said: “Clearly.” Coun Quigg has led the borough’s 16-strong group of councillors since he joined Reform in September 2025 and Reform are now second behind Labour in terms of numbers. He has consistently argued his party has the mandate to run the local authority based on strong election results b This week, town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Coun Quigg’s deputy Mark Wilkinson has taken over on an interim basis while a new leader is selected over the coming weeks

candidates.evidence_text: Wigan Four-bed house can be built in garden of Shevington bungalow after concerns addressed Previous plans for a larger property at the site were thrown out by planners Comments News Chris Gee Local democracy reporter 15:49, 09 Sep 2026 View Image The Planning permission has been granted for a four-bed detached house to be built in the back garden of an existing bungalow A meeting of Wigan council planning committee considered the proposal for the rear portion of a garden of an existing detached bungalow on Gathurst Lane, Shevington The committee heard the bungalow to the front of the site would be retained and a new two-storey, four-bedroom home with an attached garage would be built on the plot The council received 12 objections to the plans claiming over development and that the home would be out of character Other objections included loss of light, overshadowing and visual dominance, loss of privacy and overlooking and ecological and environmental concerns

candidates.evidence_text: Salford Royal hospital Girl, 13, born without hair 'left in tears' after being stripped of funding at Salford Royal "We live in a cruel world, and people stare and say things" Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer and Camilla Foster PA Real Lif A mum said she was left in tears after discovering she could no longer afford specialist wigs for her daughter, who was born without hair Ceri Williams said her 13 year old daughter Kizzi-Rae's hair "grows like fluff and then disappears", and has been receiving vouchers that fully covered the cost of two specialist wigs per year – worth £1,250 each – since she was three years old However, she recently received a letter telling her that because Kizzi-Rae has now been referred back to Wrexham Maelor Hospital from Salford Royal, she is now only entitled to two £100 vouchers a year, leaving the family £2,300 out of pocket A spokesperson from the Northern Care Alliance NHS Foundation Trust, which operates Salford Royal hospital , explained the decision followed a review of the service that led to patients living outside the local area being transitioned to their local healthcare providers "When I first received the letter I cried. With the cost of living as it is, putting food on the table each week is hard enough, and when this happened I just thought wow, what am I going to do?" the hairdresser and mother of three from Hope near Wrexham said

The issue affected 15 airports across the country, including Manchester Nats confirmed the system had been restored late on Tuesday night, with Manchester Airport able to run its usual service on Wednesday. This could see a new indoor arena built, thousands of new homes, and millions of pounds of investment Earlier this week, leaders of Oldham ’s various political parties gave the thumbs up for the creation of a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC ), a partnership between Oldham council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) that will look to fuel further growth in th Those plans have also now been backed by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig , subject to GMCA approval later this month The MDC in Oldham has been modelled off the one created in Stockport which is regarded as a blueprint for delivering town centre regeneration in the UK . The council leader there Coun Mark Roberts recently described the MDC as a ‘rocketbooster’ that has driven investment forward, If approved by the GMCA, the proposed MDC for Oldham will go to the UK Government and Parliament for approval. candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police 'Grossly inappropriate' messages sent by GMP officer to domestic abuse victim A ruling has been published after a misconduct hearing Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:10, 10 Sep 2026 View Image Greater Manchester Police A Greater Manchester Police officer sent 'grossly inappropriate' messages to a vulnerable victim of domestic abuse. The force's Chief Constable, Sir Stephen Watson, ruled Masood Meah would have been sacked over his actions had he not already resigned as a constable A misconduct hearing took place at GMP headquarters on July 14, with Sir Stephen's ruling now published In it, he said former PC Meah first came into contact with the woman during the course of his duties. He was said to have actively 'followed' and submitted 'commentary and emojis' relating to the woman on social media over a 'protracted period' Mr Meah was warned off by a friend of hers, but the ruling says he 'continued to engage' and responses to her posts 'included various emojis and commentary which can only be interpreted as intimately familiar and designed to flatter' Sir Stephen said he found that in his view, the former officer was 'apparently seeking or encouraging some form of emotional or sexual relationship with a highly vulnerable person'

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Once ruled by Romans, a forgotten corner of Oldham has been transformed into UK first Ahead of an opening next week, people have been given a first glimpse at a major new visitor attraction in Oldham Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy A major project ‘unlike anything else in the UK’ is about to open in the heart of Oldham after nearly £13m was spent transforming the area The whole Northern Roots site covers around 160 acres to the south of Oldham town centre next to Alexandra Park. Part of the site was once an old Roman road, the Brook Mill used to dominate the area, and for around five decades, it was used for landfill Now it is entering a new chapter of its history with the area’s new urban farm, considered the largest in the UK , preparing to open its doors next week on September 19 for the first time. The project has been about five years in the making and the Manchester Evening News was giv People will enter through a woodland walkway lit during the darker winter months where people can ‘leave the world behind them and have this really magical experience’. The woodland then opens out into a large green space with views of the Peak District and the urban farm at the A large visitor centre which will offer meeting spaces, a café run by acclaimed chef Mary-Ellen McTague , a large play area, as well as the urban farm itself. There will also be a forestry skills centre on site

This comes two days after other party leaders were reportedly told Councillor Lewis Quigg was being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader in the borough. However, Coun Quigg has denied the claims, initially telling the Manchester Evening News he would not ‘confirm nor deny silly allegat He later said the claims are ‘just nonsense really’ and ‘just gossip and hearsay’. When asked to confirm whether he was still leader on September 9, Coun Quigg said: “Clearly.” Coun Quigg has led the borough’s 16-strong group of councillors since he joined Reform in September 2025 and Reform are now second behind Labour in terms of numbers. He has consistently argued his party has the mandate to run the local authority based on strong election results b This week, town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Coun Quigg’s deputy Mark Wilkinson has taken over on an interim basis while a new leader is selected over the coming weeks

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed by partners hoping to bring forward a massive development which would ‘create a new neighbourhood’ and transform much of the south of Bolton A partnership agreement has been agreed between organisations including Bolton council, Peel Land and the borough’s NHS trust to move forward the Health Innovation Bolton (HIB) initiative which would have a capital investment of £520M The group described it as a £1 billion catalyst project which ‘puts health and wellbeing at the heart of a 700-acre economic and community development’ The scheme includes 200,000 sqm of employment, R&D and health floorspace alongside more than 2,000 new homes Bolton’s council leader Akhtar Zaman described the huge project as ‘an ideal fit for Bolton’s ongoing regeneration’

candidates.evidence_text: His old boss, Bev Craig, has just been elected as Greater Manchester mayor. And the man who used to hold her position, Andy Burnham , is now Prime Minister. Coun Bridges hopes these two powerful Labour figures can help him to carry out his ambitions for Manchester He has been speaking to local democracy reporter Declan Carey about his plans for Strangeways prison, affordable housing and tackling homelessness A former council estate kid who grew up in the Black Country, Coun Bridges came to Manchester for university in 2005 and never left. He has made his home here, got married here, became a parent here View 7 Images Garry Bridges (Image: Sean Hansford | Manchester Evening News) He claims his lifelong love of West Brom proves he’s no “glory hunter”, while his parents’ hard-working attitude and efforts to train while raising children means he understands the struggles many Mancunians face daily He says a belief that “poverty is not inevitable” has been a driving factor in his life. “People can and with the right help, should, have high aspirations for themselves,” he says

Communities there have been plagued by adverse weather over the years, with more than 700 homes dam The incident also impacted multiple businesses and critical infrastructure such as the Bury waste water treatment works and electricity substations. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has prison sentence increased Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 15:13, 09 Sep 2026 Updated 15:21, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Stacey S A mother who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' Stacey Sharples, 31, from Farnworth in Bolton , made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and partners, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019 when she was aged between 18 and 24. Sharples admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice at Bolton Crown Court in March and was jailed for four-and-a-hal The Attorney General referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal and on Wednesday judges increased the term to seven years. An estimated 264 hours of police time and around £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard Sharples repeated her allegations in lengthy video-recorded interviews but police found many inconsistencies in her accounts

Julie Kershaw, 58, was called to the field where she keeps 13-year-old Frank after someone found him shaking uncontrollably and barely able to walk As he lay on the grass in Rochdale , Greater Manchester, Julie feared Frank would not survive the night - believing that campers fed him human food Julie said: "With the state he was in, I didn't think he was going to be alive in the morning. He was really shaking and couldn't walk." Julie does not know exactly what Frank ate, but is convinced he was fed something dangerous by visitors because he has lived safely in the same field throughout his life Frank was discovered in distress by 13-year-old Freya and her mum Rachel while they were out walking. They saw the horse suddenly collapse, roll onto his side and begin breathing heavily as his whole body shook

The Attorney General, Ellie Reeves KC MP, has issued a statement after the sentence of Stacey Sharples was referred to the cou Sharples, from Farnworth, Bolton , made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and partners, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019 when she was aged between 18 and 24. Sharples admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice at Bolton Crown Court in March and was jailed for four-and-a-hal The Attorney General referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal and on Wednesday, judges increased her jail term to seven years. The issue affected 15 airports across the country, including Manchester Nats confirmed the system had been restored late on Tuesday night, with Manchester Airport able to run its usual service on Wednesday. Dozens of flights were delayed throughout the day however , while British Airways had cancelled some of its flights to Heathrow as it recovered f Most flights are expected to run as normal and on time today, but some cancellations and lengthy delays are expected. candidates.evidence_text: Oldham New arena and thousands of new homes in 'rocketbooster' plan for Oldham Town hall bosses are keen to stress the impact will be felt across the borough with promises of major investment Comments News Edward Barnes Local Democracy Reporter 06:12, A new ‘rocketbooster’ could turbo-charge major changes in Oldham over the next decade. This could see a new indoor arena built, thousands of new homes, and millions of pounds of investment Earlier this week, leaders of Oldham ’s various political parties gave the thumbs up for the creation of a Mayoral Development Corporation (MDC ), a partnership between Oldham council and the Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) that will look to fuel further growth in th Those plans have also now been backed by Greater Manchester Mayor Bev Craig , subject to GMCA approval later this month The MDC in Oldham has been modelled off the one created in Stockport which is regarded as a blueprint for delivering town centre regeneration in the UK . The council leader there Coun Mark Roberts recently described the MDC as a ‘rocketbooster’ that has driven investment forward, If approved by the GMCA, the proposed MDC for Oldham will go to the UK Government and Parliament for approval. If everything goes according to plan, Oldham council hopes to set up the MDC in early 2027

candidates.evidence_text: Greater Manchester Police 'Grossly inappropriate' messages sent by GMP officer to domestic abuse victim A ruling has been published after a misconduct hearing Comments News Paul Britton Reporter 06:10, 10 Sep 2026 View Image Greater Manchester Police A Greater Manchester Police officer sent 'grossly inappropriate' messages to a vulnerable victim of domestic abuse. The force's Chief Constable, Sir Stephen Watson, ruled Masood Meah would have been sacked over his actions had he not already resigned as a constable A misconduct hearing took place at GMP headquarters on July 14, with Sir Stephen's ruling now published In it, he said former PC Meah first came into contact with the woman during the course of his duties. He was said to have actively 'followed' and submitted 'commentary and emojis' relating to the woman on social media over a 'protracted period' Mr Meah was warned off by a friend of hers, but the ruling says he 'continued to engage' and responses to her posts 'included various emojis and commentary which can only be interpreted as intimately familiar and designed to flatter' Sir Stephen said he found that in his view, the former officer was 'apparently seeking or encouraging some form of emotional or sexual relationship with a highly vulnerable person'

Part of the site was once an old Roman road, the Brook Mill used to dominate the area, and for around five decades, it was used for landfill Now it is entering a new chapter of its history with the area’s new urban farm, considered the largest in the UK , preparing to open its doors next week on September 19 for the first time. The project has been about five years in the making and the Manchester Evening News was giv People will enter through a woodland walkway lit during the darker winter months where people can ‘leave the world behind them and have this really magical experience’. The woodland then opens out into a large green space with views of the Peak District and the urban farm at the A large visitor centre which will offer meeting spaces, a café run by acclaimed chef Mary-Ellen McTague , a large play area, as well as the urban farm itself. There will also be a forestry skills centre on site

candidates.evidence_text: Oldham Oldham Reform boss says he's still in charge despite claims he is being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader and other party leaders were rep Oldham Reform’s boss says claims he is no longer in the post are ‘just gossip and hearsay’. This comes two days after other party leaders were reportedly told Councillor Lewis Quigg was being replaced Multiple town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Oldham council’s Reform UK group is looking to elect a new leader in the borough. However, Coun Quigg has denied the claims, initially telling the Manchester Evening News he would not ‘confirm nor deny silly allegat He later said the claims are ‘just nonsense really’ and ‘just gossip and hearsay’. When asked to confirm whether he was still leader on September 9, Coun Quigg said: “Clearly.” Coun Quigg has led the borough’s 16-strong group of councillors since he joined Reform in September 2025 and Reform are now second behind Labour in terms of numbers. He has consistently argued his party has the mandate to run the local authority based on strong election results b This week, town hall sources have told the Manchester Evening News Coun Quigg’s deputy Mark Wilkinson has taken over on an interim basis while a new leader is selected over the coming weeks

Mr Marsden went to investigate and found a large fire in their rented end-of-terrace home in Bury He and his wife were able to escape the blaze, but their house was severely damaged and nine months on, remains uninhabitable. The unknown man smashed a window before Lynam poured petrol inside. An ‘explosion’ was caused and the pair fled Lynam was caught after DNA from a balaclava which he discarded nearby was traced to him. candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Plans advance on £520M scheme to build homes and employment space on 700 acres close to Bolton hospital Partners behind the scheme said ‘no comparable site in Greater Manchester offers the same combination of hospital adjacency, medical school An agreement has been signed by partners hoping to bring forward a massive development which would ‘create a new neighbourhood’ and transform much of the south of Bolton A partnership agreement has been agreed between organisations including Bolton council, Peel Land and the borough’s NHS trust to move forward the Health Innovation Bolton (HIB) initiative which would have a capital investment of £520M The group described it as a £1 billion catalyst project which ‘puts health and wellbeing at the heart of a 700-acre economic and community development’ The scheme includes 200,000 sqm of employment, R&D and health floorspace alongside more than 2,000 new homes Bolton’s council leader Akhtar Zaman described the huge project as ‘an ideal fit for Bolton’s ongoing regeneration’

candidates.evidence_text: Flooding Flood defences close to where 700 homes were damaged moves towards final 7-month phase More than 700 homes damaged in the catastrophic Boxing Day floods of 2015 Comments News Hannah Richardson 15:40, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Flooding on Miller Huge floodgates are set to be installed along the River Irwell over the coming months The project, led by the Environment Agency, is the final phase of a scheme to help reduce flood risk along a six kilometre stretch of the river in the Radcliffe and Redvales areas. Communities there have been plagued by adverse weather over the years, with more than 700 homes dam The incident also impacted multiple businesses and critical infrastructure such as the Bury waste water treatment works and electricity substations. The area experienced further flooding during Storm Ciara in February 2020 In this event, road closures would be implemented to allow the gates to be closed and diversion roads would be put in place The installation is expected to take around seven months to complete, with work expected to begin next month. Temporary traffic lights are to be set up at junctions either side of the bridge to allow work to be carried out safely

candidates.evidence_text: Bolton Woman who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has prison sentence increased Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' News PA and Paul Britton Reporter 15:13, 09 Sep 2026 Updated 15:21, 09 Sep 2026 View Image Stacey S A mother who falsely accused 10 men of raping her has had her prison sentence increased by two-and-a-half years after Court of Appeal judges ruled her original term was 'unduly lenient' Stacey Sharples, 31, from Farnworth in Bolton , made false reports causing men to be held in custody at police stations, lose jobs and partners, and be separated from their children She met the men from Greater Manchester on Facebook and dating apps Plenty of Fish and Badoo between 2013 and 2019 when she was aged between 18 and 24. Sharples admitted 10 counts of perverting the course of justice at Bolton Crown Court in March and was jailed for four-and-a-hal The Attorney General referred the sentence to the Court of Appeal and on Wednesday judges increased the term to seven years. An estimated 264 hours of police time and around £50,000 were wasted in months-long investigations, the court heard Sharples repeated her allegations in lengthy video-recorded interviews but police found many inconsistencies in her accounts

Julie Kershaw, 58, was called to the field where she keeps 13-year-old Frank after someone found him shaking uncontrollably and barely able to walk As he lay on the grass in Rochdale , Greater Manchester, Julie feared Frank would not survive the night - believing that campers fed him human food Julie said: "With the state he was in, I didn't think he was going to be alive in the morning. Credit: ITV News A major NHS trust has declared a critical incident as more than 350 operating theatre staff begin a series of 24-hour strikes across four hospitals Workers including nurses, clinical support workers, and housekeepers at Salford Royal, Royal Oldham , Rochdale Infirmary, and Fairfield Hospital in Bury are walking out on 24, 26, and 28 August It follows similar strike action taken by staff across the same four hospital sites in June The dispute focuses on the trust using an external agency, NHS Professionals, to manage overtime shifts Trade union UNISON claims this system forces some staff to earn less than a standard shift rate, leaving workers out of pocket by more than £80 per shift when covering staff shortages UNISON Regional Organiser Kevin Dolan claims trust bosses show a "lack of leadership" after an offer was reportedly withdrawn before talks began

candidates.evidence_text: Friday 31 July 2026 at 11:11pm More than two million voters were eligible to vote in the Greater Manchester mayoral by-election as counting getsunderway. Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Law firm Trowers & Hamlins is also among those on the tenant roster The expansion follows a wider programme of works at 55 Princess Street, including the overhaul of the building’s reception and communal areas and revamping office accommodation throughout the property With the repositioning programme now complete, Seneca Property has launched the final two available fourth-floor suites, comprising 3,725 sq ft and 4,660 sq ft. The fourth floor has had £500,000 invested in improvements

candidates.evidence_text: Death threats, gangsters, and smashed up Ferraris: forget Manchesterism — this is Oldhamism Take the last few years as an example. Since 2001 and as recently as January the town’s politicians have seen a well-documented spate of petrol bombings: of councillors’ houses, councillors’ cars, and the cars of wannabe councillors. Famous among them is the 2021 petrol bombing o That was the day Oldham Council tried, and failed, for the fifth time running, to muster enough cross-party support to elect a new leader — a position left vacant by Shah since May after a three year stint. The council’s top lawyer has now declared them to be breaking the law. Of Animosity and fear (due to the petrol bombings) run rampant among the parties. None of them have enough councillors to run the borough themselves; between them they cannot come to a consensus When reporting on this story, two of Oldham’s party leaders actually broke down in tears in front of me. Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. On Monday 17th August, Tameside Magistrates’ Court granted an order requiring the removal of the encampment The site was vacated later that day. A significant amount of waste was left behind, which has now been removed by the Council’s cleansing team

candidates.lead: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture
candidates.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . Earlier this year, local creatives were invited to apply for a Town of Culture micro-commission. There were 84 applications, with 13 projects chosen to receive funding Some of the successful artists and groups recently came together to mark the start of the programme. Not everyone was able to attend, but all 13 projects will play an important part in Oldham’s Town of Culture year The Oldham Panorama, a famous view of the town created in 1876, is 150 years old this year. Isobel and Fay will reimagine it for today using patchwork and running-stitch embroidery Local people will be invited to add buildings and places that are important to them, using old clothes and fabric from home

candidates.lead: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council
candidates.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

candidates.evidence_text: A 19th century manor house in Rochdale, which has lain empty for decades, has been transformed into a café, which will formally open this weekend Nestled in the heart of Denehurst Park, the café will occupy the ground floor of Denehurst House and visitors can see it for themselves when it formally opens its doors this Saturday (5 September) More than just a café, the new venue will be managed and run by local Community Interest Company, Get Together After Serving (GTAS), and will be staffed entirely by former armed forces personnel and their families Set up by Rochdale residents, Adam Trennery, Wayne Traynor and Wayne Simms, GTAS aims to support the local veteran community in a number of ways, including through wellbeing programmes and local events and get-togethers Customers can expect café favourites like hot and cold sandwiches, cakes, breakfasts and tea and coffee, alongside generous opening hours and honest prices. The team is also hoping to team up with other local businesses to do specials on Fridays, like curry, pizza and pies. With The building has been transformed by its owners, Rochdale Borough Council, who commissioned local builders, H Bell and Sons, alongside interior design specialists, to renovate the building while honouring its period features, which include ornate coving and bay windows

candidates.lead: Another Bolton primary school is set to join the growing number that are making it safer and easier for children to walk, bike or wheel to school
candidates.evidence_text: Child safe travel scheme adds another school – Bolton Council Published: Wednesday, 9th Sep 2026 Another Bolton primary school is set to join the growing number that are making it safer and easier for children to walk, bike or wheel to school. The Ferns Primary Academy on Plodder Lane will start operating Schools Streets from Monday, September 14. It means that on days when the school is open, access to Westend Street will be controlled at school drop off and pick up times. Residents, workers, school staff and emergency responders will still be able to get in and out of the street, with school staff and trained volunteers on hand to let the necessary vehicles through. Controlled access will operate in the morning from 8:20am to 9:00am, and in the afternoon from 2:30pm to 3:15pm. This latest School Streets project brings the total operating in Bolton to five, with four starting earlier this year. More widely, the number of Schools Streets across Greater Manchester has reached over 40, while London has over 700. In Bolton, School Streets are in place at: Kearsley West Primary School St. Bedes Primary Academy Sharples Primary School The Gates Primary School The Ferns Primary School Before bringing in School Streets the schools trialled them for a day, with feedback from parents, residents and children up to 90 per cent positive. Among the most common reasons were better safety for the children and a calmer environment during school opening time. Across the UK, travelling to and from school is the most dangerous time of day for road accidents involving children, with almost three-quarters of accidents happening between 8am and 9am and 3pm and 7pm. Bolton Council’s Executive Member for Children’s Services, Cllr Rabiya Jiva, said: “It’s encouraging to see that the success of School Streets across the UK is now being seen in Bolton too. “Kids love getting to school and back home under their own steam, and of course it’s vital that we keep them safe while they are doing it thanks to School Streets.” For more information about School Streets in Bolton, visit www.bolton.gov.uk/road-safety/school-streets Cookie Consent by Free Privacy Policy website

candidates.evidence_text: A shop in Leigh town centre has been closed for three months following repeated seizures of illicit tobacco products Wigan Council’s Trading Standards team, in partnership with Greater Manchester Police, secured the closure order for Shop & Save on Bradshawgate after concerns were raised about illegal sales Following an investigation by Trading Standards, a three-month closure order was approved at Wigan and Leigh Magistrates Court on Thursday, 3rd September Councillor Kevin Anderson, portfolio holder for police, crime and civil contingencies said: "This closure order yet again demonstrates our commitment to tackling illegal trading and protecting our communities across Wigan Borough “Traders who engage in this kind of activity will not be allowed to continue breaking the law, and we will continue working with partners to investigate reports of illicit sales and take robust action where unlawful activity is identified.” Over the course of two months, Trading Standards officers seized 7,380 sticks of illicit cigarettes and four kilograms of illicit hand rolling tobacco, which was concealed in elaborate hides within the premises

candidates.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

History, power and empire collide in Button Up! – a major new exhibition from the world-leading artist and activist Ai Weiwei . Internationally renowned artist and activist Ai Weiwei turns his critical gaze to the last 200 years of global history with this major new exhibition. Monumental in scale and ambition, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! is the artist’s most expansive presentation in the North to date.. Ai Weiwei is known around the world for his uncompromising artistic vision and political activism. From a childhood in exile to surviving secret detention in China, his remarkable life and career have led him to global prominence. Using sculpture, installation, film, photography and architecture, his work is unafraid to ask urgent, critical questions.. In Button Up! , the artist turns his lens on two centuries of Chinese and British relations. Taking inspiration from Manchester, a city at the heart of the Industrial Revolution, Button Up! explores how historic systems of trade, empire and exploitation resonate in today’s humanitarian and political crises.. Conceived as a total environment, Ai Weiwei: Button Up! brings together new and existing large-scale works on display in the UK for the first time. The monumental installation features porcelain, cotton, glass, bronze and even buttons and toy bricks. Each material contains a story of human invention and consumption. Together, they paint a picture of globalisation.. Both global and personal, the title Button Up! is a playful poke at the artist’s ongoing battle with censorship. The exhibition also features the world premiere of a new body of work created especially for the vast spaces of the Warehouse – Eight-Nation Alliance Flags made from millions of buttons, as well as a new version of History Of Bombs made entirely from toy bricks.. The new commissions sit alongside large-scale works by the artist which are going on show in the UK for the first time: Law of the Journey (2017), a 47m long inflatable migrant boat containing hundreds of human figures and the artist’s largest artwork to date; Wang Family Ancestral Hall (2015), a Ming dynasty ancestral temple reassembled from 1,500 individual wooden pieces ; and La Commedia Umana (2017-21), a black Murano glass chandelier made up of over 2,000 pieces and weighing nearly 3 tonnes. Also on show is Circle of Animals/Zodiac Heads (2010), a re-envisioning of the twelve animals of the Chinese zodiac.. Button Up! immerses visitors in Ai Weiwei’s fearless interrogation of the forces past and present that drive today’s injustices – while championing art’s enduring power to challenge and inspire.. . . . “I’m not interested in making very big things just for the sake of it. But in Manchester, that wonderful Warehouse space calls for monumental work. Visiting the city for this exhibition – the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution – and reflecting on Britain’s global territorial expansion made me realise I had to explore that history and understand how it connects to the forces driving today’s wars and global crises. The world today is deeply divided, with tragedy all around. Understanding history goes hand in hand with standing up for truth and justice.”. Ai Weiwei. . . Explore. . Ai Weiwei | Dream Space . Павел Дедищев - комик с ярко выраженным собственным стилем, в котором сочетаются честность, дерзость и умение подмечать детали, знакомые каждому. Его стендап строится на живых наблюдениях, бытовых историях и неожиданных поворотах, которые превращают обычные ситуации в мощные комедийные моменты. Дедищев говорит прямо, не сглаживает углы и именно этим вызывает у зрителей тот самый взрывной смех. Address: Big Belly Comedy Club, Unit 6 & 7, 30 Stamford St, London SE1 9LQ Doors: 19:00 Start: 19:45 End: 21:30 Мы работаем по принципу first come, first served, а именно, кто пришел раньше, то и занял лучшее место. 18+ P.S. PINK's Summer Open Mic is being put on by local guitar shop Rigby Music, with covers and originals welcome from anyone who wants to give it a go Alongside the music, fellow Hilton House residents Spearpoint Vintage are setting up a pop-up of pieces from their collection, available to buy on the night, with the chance to book in for a future appointment at their showroom too It's a relaxed one — no pressure, just a room of people who like music and a rail of good vintage to pick through between sets Where: PINK, Hilton House, Lord Street, Stockport SK1 3NA When: Wednesday 5 August 2026, 6:45pm–10pm Want to perform? Email admin@rigbymusic.co.uk Know of an open mic or pop-up we should be covering? Let us know — we're always up for a Wednesday night out in the borough

candidates.evidence_text: With the future of devolution, AI policy and regional growth firmly on the agenda, Manchester Digital Managing Director and UK Tech Cluster Group Chair Katie Gallagher OBE recently spoke to The Startup Coalition about what the next phase could mean for Manchester and the wider No From the potential impact of greater devolved powers in Manchester to the role of No.10 North, Katie explores how national and regional government can work more effectively with the tech sector - and why the North’s different tech ecosystems need to be better connected rather tha Greater devolution will be positive for Manchester’s tech ecosystem. It already has a strong tech base and devolution gives us a chance to align policy, funding and delivery more closely with what is happening on the ground To do that well, Combined Authorities and others need to understand that ecosystems are much broader and deeper than most public-facing institutions realise, that matters if they are going to make good decisions on skills, infrastructure, procurement and innovation support AI and emerging technologies clearly need focus because their impact will be felt across every part of the economy, but policy needs to keep pace with how those technologies are being used by businesses. Government and Combined Authorities will have more impact if they understand The new Digital Campus in Manchester is a good example of where this could become practical; a larger concentration of public sector digital capability in Manchester should create new routes for startups and scaleups to work with the government. It should mean earlier engagement

evidence_packet.evidence_text: A special evening celebrating one of Manchester’s most influential musicians, Vini Reilly and his post-punk project The Durutti Column, comes to Albert Hall this November Fresh from sold-out Southbank Centre performances, a unique ensemble will reinterpret key works from The Durutti Column’s remarkable six-decade career in Reilly’s home city on Thu 19 Nov Presenting the one-night-only For Vini show is producer Keir Stewart, who has worked with Reilly and drummer Bruce Mitchell since 1998’s Time Was Gigantic… When We Were Kids album For the performance, Stewart (guitar, bass, samples, keys) is joined by The Durutti Column collaborators Sam Morris (French horn), Caoilfhionn Rose (vocals and piano) and Liz Rossi (violin and piano) Audiences can expect to hear material that spans releases on Factory Records through to tracks from Renascent , creating a rare and immersive live experience that honours one of Manchester’s most singular musical voices, one recently cited as a key influence on Harry Styles’ late Tickets go on sale Fri 11 Sep. The menu will evolve regularly, keeping the offering fresh and exciting while making Each course at Arcadian will be served by the chefs themselves, including small plates such as coal-seared beef tartare, served with bone marrow toast and cured egg yolk, alongside fire-roasted prawns with grilled lemon, garlic and ‘nduja butter

candidates.evidence_text: Manchester Central Library , Manchester Until 20 December 2026 Additional information Always double check opening hours with the venue before making a special visit Manchester has always been a city with stories to tell. This guided walking tour will bring those stories to life. Led by a local expert, the experience is set to be a lively introduction to the people, places and ideas that have shaped one of the UK’s most influential cities The tour will begin at Manchester Central Library, that impossible to miss, grand circular landmark on St Peter’s Square. The neoclassical design has made it one of the city’s most-loved buildings, holding thousands of stories in its walls and on its shelves. The square itself ha From here, the tour takes you through the city’s heart, down the colourful streets of the Gay Village and the calming Sackville Gardens. It is here that you will see the monuments that honour Manchester’s role in the fight for equality and the city’s pioneering LGBTQ+ community a This guided tour is filled with monuments and tales from many moons ago. The Medieval Quarter is the perfect place to soak in all that history. It is here where you will see the oldest public library in the English-speaking world, Chetham’s Library . Housed in a beautiful sandsto During all this walking, your guide will point out local street art, hidden corners and stories you’d easily miss on your own. Tales of suffragettes, reformers, musicians and everyday Mancunians who’ve all left their mark on the city in their own way

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Altrincham Market and market house, part restaurant, part market, part town square. Food, drink, shopping and more Altrincham ‪Market House. Eat, meet, drink, shop, watch, talk, listen, laugh. Come in, be yourself and if you like it bring your friends! Altrincham’s charter dates back to 1290, it’s location at the intersection of the Cheshire farm belt and the commercial commuter zone of Manchester means the town has a long and important history. Altrincham market is now at the heart of the regeneration of ‘the modern market tow The covered market hosts regional food producers, vintage fashion and furniture, home & garden and contemporary craft on a Tuesday, Friday, Saturday and Sunday Altrincham Market House Opening Hours Tues-Sat : 9am-10pm Sun : 9am-6pm Mon : Closed The Outdoor Market (Shopping) Tues: 8am-3pm Fri: 8am-3pm Sat: 8am-4pm Sun: 10am-4pm Altrincham Market House is home to award-winning independent quality food operators. These include the following: Honest Crust – wood fired pizza “among the country’s best”. Tender Cow who serve rare breed flat iron steak and chips. Jack in the Box selling fantastic craft beers. candidates.evidence_text: Football UEFA Champions League Man United add eight players to Champions League squad as final decisions confirmed for Sabah clash Michael Carrick has confirmed the players who will be available to him for the Champions League clash against Sabah at Old Trafford on Thursday Manchester United have made eight additions to their Champions League squad after confirming their B-list players ahead of the opening clash against Sabah. Michael Carrick's side return to Europe's top competition almost three years on from finishing bottom of their group in 2023 United confirmed their 25-man Champions League squad last week, with young stars Kobbie Mainoo and Leny Yoro not included. That squad is locked in for the league phase of competition but both players are still available for selection due to the B list Players born on or after 1 January 2005, who have been eligible to play for the club for two consecutive years since turning 15 (or three years including a loan spell), are allowed to be added to the B list. This list can be updated across the tournament, with players required to Get the best United news, updates and analysis straight to your Inbox courtesy of the Manchester Evening News! United have wasted little time placing Yoro and Mainoo on this list alongside six other players. Left back Harry Amass, central defender Daniel Armer, Darren Fletcher's sons, Jack and Tyler Fletcher, midfielder Jim Thwaites, and the promising Shea Lacey have all been named ahead

Его главный талант — превращать народные мотивы в современное искусство, не теряя их подлинной силы. Вместе с легендарным “Wedding and Funera Окунитесь в этот балканский водоворот прямо в самом сердце Лондона! candidates.evidence_text: Arcadian , the latest restaurant from award-winning chef Andrew Sheridan and Open Restaurant Group will officially open its doors at 5pm today in the heart of Didsbury village Marking the fast-growing hospitality group’s eighth restaurant to date, Arcadian is its first site in Greater Manchester, bringing a new fire-led dining experience to Didsbury, with bookings open now here At the heart of Arcadian’s kitchen is a bespoke open-fire grill, from which the restaurant takes its name, with every element of the menu shaped by cooking over wood, charcoal and open flame. The 74-cover restaurant also features a private dining room for up to 12 guests, while t The restaurant focuses on exceptional produce sourced from trusted farmers, growers and suppliers, with classical techniques allowing the quality of the ingredients to take centre stage. The menu will evolve regularly, keeping the offering fresh and exciting while making the most Each course at Arcadian will be served by the chefs themselves, including small plates such as coal-seared beef tartare, served with bone marrow toast and cured egg yolk, alongside fire roasted prawns with grilled lemon, garlic and ‘nduja butter From the fire, mains to choose from include Warrendale Wagyu Ribeye, served with chilli miso butter, beef-fat chips and sesame. There’s also grilled monkfish tail with shellfish butter and charred fennel, as well as whole piri-piri chicken and a wood-fired cauliflower. For guests

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Say hello to Sister Moon, a beautiful new restaurant bringing a taste of Southeast Asia to Manchester city centre It’s the latest addition to Manchester’s Treehouse Hotel, which opened last year transforming a huge building at the end of Deansgate This is the final chapter of its new opening, and it might be our favourite one yet Sister Moon is the new project from acclaimed chef Sam Grainger who you’ll know from Madre, among others Sam is working alongside Luke Cowdrey and Justin Crawford (Electric Chair, Volta, Freight Island) at Sister Moon, a Southeast Asian BBQ concept inspired by his time cooking with a local family in Thailand All the dishes are cooked on open fire, including dishes like the fried pork skewers with banana ketchup and the grilled prawns with crispy chilli and garlic
